final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT (draft for outside counsel review)
EXECUTIVE BRIEFING MEMORANDUM
To: Lars Engebretsen (CEO); Brian Hsu; Fiona Driscoll. From: Legal & Compliance. Re: CPRA/CCPA enforcement exposure, CPPA Inquiry (Case No. CPPA-ENF-2025-01847), remediation priorities.
Timing note: analyzed as of Feb. 10, 2025 (response due Mar. 18, 2025); that date has passed as of Oct. 2026, so see Section 8.

1. BOTTOM LINE
- CHG has clear, documented violations in five areas, and the Inquiry Letter will likely expose them. The document requests (policies, recipients, downstream deletion evidence) reach the systemic problems.
- Highest risk: (1) no honoring of Global Privacy Control (GPC) and no opt-out of sale/sharing, (2) a dark-pattern consent banner, (3) late deletions with no downstream deletion mechanism, (4) pre-CPRA vendor contracts that likely convert vendors into "third parties", (5) an undisclosed, monetized loyalty program and undisclosed sensitive geolocation sharing.
- Recommendation: meet the Mar. 18 deadline with a complete, accurate, outside-counsel-managed response; start remediation now; budget about $430,000-$500,000 plus the ADN/Prism revenue and ad-efficiency scenarios in Section 6.
- Realistic exposure is low-to-mid seven figures for a negotiated resolution if CHG remediates and cooperates. The multi-million theoretical maxima in the supplied materials are not reliable and should not go to the board unqualified.

2. LEGAL FRAMEWORK (binding unless noted)
- CCPA as amended by CPRA, Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq.; CPPA regulations, Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7000 et seq. (binding). CPPA press releases, FAQs and enforcement advisories are persuasive/interpretive, not law.
- Penalties: 1798.155 and 1798.199.55 allow administrative fines per violation; 1798.199.90 gives the Attorney General concurrent civil-penalty authority. The documents use $2,500/$7,500; the CPI-adjusted figures effective Jan. 1, 2025 are $2,663 and $7,988 (intentional violations, or minors under 16). Limitations: five years (1798.199.70).
- No mandatory cure period. The CPPA may decline to investigate or allow cure (1798.199.45), and must consider "good faith cooperation" in setting any fine (1798.199.100). That makes early remediation and candor legally relevant, not just tactical.

3. ISSUES, ASSESSMENT AND PRIORITY
A. GPC / opt-out of sale and sharing (CRITICAL). 1798.120, 1798.135, regs 7025-7026. All 23 tags fire regardless of the Sec-GPC signal; no "Do Not Sell or Share" link or opt-out exists (M-11 and CEO thread). CTO estimates 8-12 weeks, not the audit's 4-6; plan on the CTO figure. Interim: suppress advertising tags for GPC browsers via tag-manager rules within days.
B. Dark-pattern banner (CRITICAL). Reg 7004: symmetry in choice; no "Reject All"; default-on toggles. Consent so obtained is not valid. Two to three weeks; the fastest fix.
C. Sale/sharing of loyalty data to ADN and Prism (CRITICAL; the board-level issue). Cross-context behavioral advertising disclosures are "sharing" (1798.140(ah)); paid disclosure is also likely a "sale" (1798.140(ad)). The internal "partner" label is legally irrelevant; classification turns on contract terms and use (regs 7050-7053). A recipient using data for its own advertising purposes is a third party. Consequences: notice at collection, privacy policy disclosure, opt-out link, honoring GPC, a third-party contract with the 1798.100(d) terms (reg 7053), and notice to third parties of opt-outs. Brian's "consumers opted into the program" argument fails: enrollment is not consent to sale/sharing, and opt-in is not the CCPA model for adults (except for the financial-incentive opt-in below); consent via a dark-pattern interface is void.
D. Financial incentive / loyalty program (HIGH; "sleeper"). 1798.125(b) and regs 7016, 7080-7081: a loyalty program that collects data in exchange for benefits requires a notice of financial incentive, a good-faith estimate of the value of the data and the method of calculation, and opt-in consent revocable at any time. The data revenue implies about $5.49 per member per year, which any value estimate must address. No notice exists. This is not yet a stated priority in the supplied materials, but it will surface the moment the Agency pulls the ADN/Prism thread.
E. Deletion timing and downstream deletion (CRITICAL; the active inquiry). 1798.105(c), 1798.130(a)(2), reg 7021-7022: confirm receipt within 10 business days; respond in 45 days; one 45-day extension only with notice within the first 45 days. For both complainants: acknowledgment at 8 business days (compliant on that point and contradicting the complaints' "no communication" allegation, subject to verifying logs), completion at 72 and 74 days, no extension notice. Without notice, the extension is unavailable, so both requests were late (days 46-74 are unexcused). CHG must also notify service providers, contractors and third parties to whom data was sold or shared (1798.105(c)). CHG cannot prove either for the nine outdated-DPA vendors and ADN/Prism.
F. Vendor contracts (CRITICAL/HIGH). 1798.100(d), 1798.140(ag), (j), reg 7051. Nine vendors lack required terms; without them they are not "service providers/contractors" and disclosure may be a sale/sharing. Two internal lists conflict: the audit's Appendix A names Maplewood, Ridgeline, Bayside, Elkhorn and Glacier Point among the nine; the CTO's Feb. 7 tracker names Northbluff, Canopy, Brackenridge, Ashgrove, Crestwood, Oakmont plus ADN, Prism and Locale Metrics. Both cannot be right. Reconcile against the actual executed contracts before anything is produced to the CPPA. Cost is $51,000 per the CTO tracker versus $45,000 in the audit. Canopy and Ashgrove (ad retargeting using data for their own purposes) and Crestwood (loyalty engine feeding ADN/Prism) are higher risk than the audit suggests; Canopy (renews Mar. 1, 2025), Prism (renewed Jan. 9, 2025) and ADN (June 14, 2025) renewal dates are negotiating leverage and decision points.
G. Sensitive personal information (HIGH). Precise geolocation is SPI (1798.140(ae)). Correction: the documents use a 1,750-foot radius; the statute (1798.140(w)) uses 1,850 feet. No change in result: Locale receives data accurate to 50 feet. Policy has no SPI disclosure, no right-to-limit link. Nuance: a limit link is not required if SPI is used only for permitted purposes (reg 7027(m)), including services performed on the business's behalf. That depends on Locale Metrics being a compliant service provider, which today it cannot be (2021 DPA, no SPI terms), and CHG pays Locale for services in exchange for the data, so a "sale" argument also exists. Fix by contract first; otherwise offer the limit link.
H. Privacy policy (CRITICAL). Last updated Mar. 2023; missing SPI, correction, retention, sharing, limit rights (1798.130(a)(5), reg 7011). Required update at least every 12 months.

4. DATA INTEGRITY PROBLEMS IN THE SUPPLIED MATERIALS (fix before relying or producing)
- Deletion count: 7,480 is 22% of all 34,000 requests, but the audit says 22% of deletion requests, and deletions were about 18,000 (Appendix B). 22% of 18,000 is about 3,960. CTO email also says 34,000 are deletion requests; they are not. At $2,663 the theoretical maximum is about $10.5M (3,960) not $18.7M; if 7,480 holds, about $19.9M. Deletion is a count of requests, and per-violation counting is the Agency's choice.
- GPC exposure: 29,250 is 15% of the 195,000 app users, not website visitors (1.62M consumers annually); the $73.1M and $487.5M figures are arithmetic on inconsistent bases. Treat them as illustrative ceilings only.
- Chronology: the audit is dated Jan. 15, 2025 yet discusses the Feb. 3 Inquiry Letter; it was revised after its date or misdated. Establish version history, because the CPPA or counsel may ask.
- Authority I could not verify: the Aug. 2024 "first GPC sweep" with $1.85M in three settlements, the Nov. 2024 dark-pattern sweep and the Oct. 15, 2024 "sharing" advisory opinion do not match public records I found. The CPPA's first announced settlement was Honda (Mar. 2025, $632,500), and its public enforcement advisories were No. 2024-01 (data minimization, Apr. 2024) and a Sept. 2024 dark-pattern advisory. The statutory analysis above does not depend on these items (sharing is defined by statute), but do not quote the settlement figures to the board until the Legal team confirms the sources.
- Hiring two FTEs may not be in the $425,000.

5. EXPOSURE (what to tell the board)
- Theoretical statutory maxima are in the tens of millions to over $100 million; they are not predictive. The CPPA has resolved matters by negotiated amounts far below.
- Benchmarks (public, post-dating the memo): CPPA: Honda $632,500 (Mar. 2025; opt-out friction, asymmetric tool, missing third-party contracts), Todd Snyder about $345,000 (2025; broken opt-out), Tractor Supply $1.35M (Sept. 2025; opt-out and GPC). The AG's Sephora $1.2M (2024) was GPC/sale. CHG has more simultaneous failures than any of these.
- Realistic range if CHG remediates and cooperates: approximately $0.5M-$2M; if the matter is expanded and found intentional or multi-issue and CHG stalls, $2M-$5M+ plus a multi-year compliance order. This is judgment for outside counsel to refine. Aggravators: knowledge since the Jan. 15, 2025 audit (continued non-compliance supports "intentional"), duration, 412,000 loyalty members, and revenue from the data.
- Business impact: ADN/Prism revenue $2.26M (2.6% of CA revenue); marketing's estimate of $3-4M of lost ad efficiency if shut off entirely is unaudited. Full shutoff is not required: only opted-out consumers and a compliant structure are needed; model opt-out scenarios of 10%, 25% and 50% of members.

6. REMEDIATION ROADMAP (cost; owner; timing)
Now (days 0-14): (1) litigation hold covering request logs, portal data, emails, tag configurations and vendor files; suspend auto-deletion; preserve the two consumers' request records even while completing their deletions (retention for legal obligations is a permitted exception, 1798.105(d)); (2) engage Oakvale Hale LLP in writing, with counsel directing any further consultant work; (3) complete both complainants' deletions, send downstream deletion instructions to every recipient, and document it; (4) GPC interim suppression of advertising tags; (5) banner redesign and "Reject All" ($62,000 UX budget).
Weeks 2-8: privacy policy rewrite with SPI, sharing, retention, correction and limit rights; "Do Not Sell or Share" and "Limit" links; notice of financial incentive and loyalty terms; opt-out infrastructure for ADN/Prism with signal propagation; backlog triage of open deletion requests (day-30 and day-40 escalation, extension notice templates); two FTEs.
Weeks 4-12: renegotiate nine DPAs (target dates in tracker are Apr. 15-June 15, 2025; ADN, Prism, Locale, Crestwood first); automated deletion workflow with vendor confirmations; geolocation consent and SPI controls; HR/employee data review (380 CA employees; exemption expired Jan. 1, 2023).
Budget: $425,000 audit estimate, plus $6,000 DPA delta, FTE salaries, and contingency; the privacy line is $340,000, so supplemental approval is needed (at least $91,000).

7. CPPA RESPONSE STRATEGY
- Hold Mar. 18 (30 business days counts to Mar. 18 only if Presidents' Day is excluded; confirm with analyst Daniela Vargas in writing). A short rolling production for item (d) beats an incomplete submission.
- Answer exactly what is asked, fully and truthfully. Narrow scope is lawful; omission that makes a statement misleading is not. Each of (a)-(d) must be correct: policy versions in force from Sept. 1, 2024; recipients of the two consumers' data must include ADN and Prism and the actual vendor list; item (d) must say what was and was not done. Do not claim contractual deletion rights CHG lacks. The Feb. 10 enforcement memo's suggestion of avoiding "unnecessary disclosure" must be applied within these limits.
- Document dated remediation; it supports 1798.199.100 mitigation.
- Privilege: be careful. Thornbury was retained by the VP of Legal, not by outside counsel, its report disclaims legal advice and any attorney-client relationship, and it is largely factual. Assume it may be producible or its privilege contested; do not rely on it, do not send it to third parties, and route future audit work through outside counsel under a written engagement. Facts are not privileged in any event. Log any withheld documents as the letter requires.

8. CURRENCY NOTE (as of Oct. 2026)
Confirm what was filed and the case status. New CCPA regulations on risk assessments, automated decisionmaking and cybersecurity audits were approved Sept. 23, 2025, effective Jan. 1, 2026 with phased obligations from 2027; the CPPA now also publishes the CPI-adjusted fines. Re-run this analysis against current law and then-current enforcement orders.

9. DECISIONS REQUESTED
(1) Approve outside counsel and litigation hold today; (2) approve interim GPC suppression and banner fix; (3) approve supplemental budget of about $430,000-$500,000; (4) direct Marketing to model ADN/Prism opt-out scenarios and prepare the financial-incentive disclosure; (5) approve submitting the response by Mar. 18 with a documented remediation timetable.
